basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Represents one condition occurrence in one organism, not the disease concept in a terminology.
Clinical status, verification status and record status are independent axes.
Remission is not cure, susceptibility is not disease, and association is not causation.
A diagnosis is an authority-qualified assertion; a single observation or test result is not a diagnosis.

may: Record a condition with a release-pinned terminology code and source.
Validate codes against the declared terminology release.
Detect probable duplicate condition records for review.
Summarise the course, stage and severity history from recorded assertions.
mustNot: Infer a condition from one observation or from genetic susceptibility.
Disclose a condition outside the authorised purpose.
Merge or delete condition records without authority.
Report a public-health case without the responsible authority.
requiresHuman: Diagnosis and verification of a condition.
Disclosure of a condition to third parties.

considerations: Health conditions are sensitive data; disclosure can cause stigma, discrimination and loss of work or insurance.
Wrong or outdated diagnoses can lead to harmful treatment.
Public-health reporting must balance community protection against individual privacy.
Animal conditions also matter for welfare and for diseases shared with people.

properties.reason: A condition is a clinical concept; severity and stage are assessments recorded about a person, not physical properties.

items: A condition record has a subject, a coded concept, clinical and verification status, onset and the asserting authority.
Often confused with a disease concept, an observation, a symptom and a diagnostic test result.
Duplicate or conflicting records for one condition.
Missed or delayed notification of a notifiable disease.
